title: Rank, alpha, DoRA, LoKr and the other adapters
hook: Every patch format in comfy/weight_adapter, as a sum you can check: what it stores, what it can reach, and what alpha means in each.

verified.claim: The lab's lora, loha, lokr, dora and factorization match ComfyUI's real functions on test tensors, largest difference 0.0. The real OFTAdapter keeps the weight's norm in a test.
adapter_maps lists LoRA, LoHa, LoKr and OFT for training, with GLoRA and BOFT commented out, while all six can load.
TrainLoraNode passes its rank widget as factor to LoKr and OFT, through create_train.
LoKr uses alpha only when a factor was itself decomposed. OFT uses alpha as a norm limit.
Train adapters ignore dora_scale, and create_train passes None, so the core trainer does not make DoRA.
The bypass docstring says bypass is designed for quantized models.
Paper titles came from the arXiv API. We read abstracts only: the claims attributed to them come from those.

unchecked: We read abstracts of the adapter papers, not the full texts, and ComfyUI's code does not cite most of them directly. Linking a code path to a paper by its method's name is our reading.
Nothing here compares picture quality. Which adapter suits which job is open and untested here.
GLoRA's and BOFT's sums were not worked through in the lab.
That bypass and a merge can differ slightly in a picture follows from the rounding in CU-212. We did not test it on a picture.
